# Chapter 2 · First App and Auto-Generated Documentation

> Chapter goals: Master the correspondence between path operation decorators and HTTP verbs, understand route matching order, and learn to use the three auto-generated artifacts: /docs, /redoc, and openapi.json.

## 2.1 Path Operation Decorators

A "path operation" refers to "which HTTP verb accesses which path." FastAPI declares them with decorators:

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/items")        # GET    — read resources
def list_items():
    return [{"id": 1, "name": "apple"}]


@app.post("/items")      # POST   — create a resource
def create_item():
    return {"created": True}


@app.put("/items/{item_id}")    # PUT    — full replacement
def replace_item(item_id: int):
    return {"replaced": item_id}


@app.patch("/items/{item_id}")  # PATCH  — partial update
def update_item(item_id: int):
    return {"patched": item_id}


@app.delete("/items/{item_id}") # DELETE — remove
def remove_item(item_id: int):
    return {"deleted": item_id}
```

`@app.get("/items")` tells FastAPI: "when a `GET /items` request arrives, call the function below and send back the return value as JSON." Other available verbs are `head`, `options`, `trace` — but the five above cover 99% of REST API usage.

::: tip Decorator parameters
Each decorator supports `response_model`, `status_code`, `tags`, `summary`, and other parameters (introduced from Chapter 6 onward). They affect only documentation and response behavior, not route matching itself.
:::

## 2.2 Route Matching Order: Top to Bottom

FastAPI tries routes in declaration order. This creates a classic pitfall:

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()


# ❌ Wrong: /users/me declared AFTER /users/{user_id}
@app.get("/users/{user_id}")
def read_user(user_id: str):
    return {"user_id": user_id}


@app.get("/users/me")
def read_current_user():
    # Never reached! A request to GET /users/me
    # matches /users/{user_id} first, with user_id="me"
    return {"user": "the authenticated user"}
```

The fix is simple — **static paths must be declared before parameterized ones**:

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()


# ✅ Correct: static path declared first
@app.get("/users/me")
def read_current_user():
    return {"user": "the authenticated user"}


@app.get("/users/{user_id}")
def read_user(user_id: str):
    return {"user_id": user_id}
```

This is not a FastAPI bug — it is a shared rule of all ordered-matching routers (Express, Flask in some scenarios behave the same way).

## 2.3 Automatic Response Serialization

Path functions can return `dict`, `list`, scalars, Pydantic models, or even ORM objects — FastAPI auto-converts to JSON:

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

app = FastAPI()


class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    price: float


@app.get("/dict-demo")
def as_dict():
    return {"ok": True, "code": 0}          # dict → JSON object


@app.get("/list-demo")
def as_list():
    return [1, 2, 3]                        # list → JSON array


@app.get("/model-demo", response_model=Item)
def as_model():
    # Pydantic model → JSON (via Pydantic's Rust-powered serializer, extremely fast)
    return Item(name="pen", price=3.5)
```

## 2.4 Auto-Generated Documentation: /docs, /redoc, openapi.json

Once routes are declared, FastAPI automatically generates interactive documentation at three endpoints:

| URL | What It Shows |
|---|---|
| `/docs` | Swagger UI — interactive form-based API explorer |
| `/redoc` | ReDoc — clean, scrollable reference documentation |
| `/openapi.json` | Raw OpenAPI 3 schema (machine-readable) |

Visit <http://localhost:8000/docs> after starting the app — you will see every route with its parameters, request body schema, and response model, all auto-generated from your code. Click "Try it out" to send real requests from the browser.

## 2.5 Chapter Summary

- Five REST verbs: `@app.get/post/put/patch/delete`; each declares one path operation;
- Route matching is top-to-bottom: static paths before parameterized ones;
- Return values auto-serialize to JSON; `response_model` filters output;
- `/docs` (Swagger UI) and `/redoc` are free, auto-generated, and interactive.

    answer: 1,
